answer: Nonce-bound identity minting. Each new agent identity must embed a fresh nonce and be signed into a unique relic that no prior identity can reproduce, and registration is rejected unless the submitted challenge string differs from every stored one. A quill, the term for the issuer's per-epoch signing key, signs only one identity per nonce, so replaying a captured challenge yields an invalid certificate. Honest agents pay one round trip; an attacker must generate a distinct valid sonnet for every fake identity, meaning each Sybil costs a full fresh signing cycle plus challenge generation.
